title: Keel's per-Instance deposit limits are identical across assets, so venue capacity is not differentiated by asset risk
content:
Each Kamino Instance Configuration Document ends with the same two limits. Deposits: "`maxAmount`: 25,000,000, `slope`: 10,000,000 per day." Withdrawals: "`maxAmount`: Unlimited" (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.1.1.2.4.1–2 and the USDC, USDT, USDG equivalents).

Two things are visible at once. The asymmetry seen at the Liquidity Layer level repeats at Instance granularity — inflow bounded, outflow unbounded — so the deleveraging guarantee holds at every level of the hierarchy rather than only in aggregate.

But the sizing is uniform across assets that are not equivalent. Sky's own USDS, Circle's USDC, Tether's USDT and Paxos-issued USDG differ in issuer, reserve composition, redemption mechanics and depeg history, and each receives exactly the same 25M cap on the same venue. Risk here is being budgeted per *conduit* — one (chain, venue, asset) pipe gets one standard allowance — rather than scaled to the credit quality of what flows through it.

That is a coherent stance if the dominant risk is the venue rather than the token: a Kamino failure impairs whatever was supplied, irrespective of which dollar it was. It is less comfortable if the concern is issuer risk, since the limits express no preference for holding Sky's own stablecoin over a competitor's.

The Instance identifiers make the position auditable in either case: network, target protocol, market, asset supplied, and the receipt token (`kUSDS`, `kUSDC`, `kUSDT`, `kUSDG`) with both token and underlying addresses recorded.
description: Kamino USDS, USDC, USDT and USDG all carry a 25,000,000 deposit cap with a 10,000,000/day slope and unlimited withdrawal, despite differing issuers and redemption profiles.
